$100 one-time usage credit Sessions up to 1 hour 20 concurrent sandboxes Default sandbox CPU and RAM

exclusions: Plan fee: Hobby $0/month; Pro $150/month; Enterprise custom with a $3,000/month minimum. Usage is billed on top. The rates above are the same on Hobby and Pro.
Which plan each size needs: Hobby includes default sandbox CPU and RAM; Pro allows custom sandbox CPU and RAM. Sessions are up to 1 hour on Hobby and up to 24 hours on Pro.
Concurrency add-ons on Pro: Pro+ 600 concurrent sandboxes +$500/month; Pro++ 1,100 concurrent +$1,000/month.
Storage: free, 10 GiB on Hobby and 20 GiB on Pro; no separate storage rate is published.
Network egress, sandbox creation and paused-sandbox retention: the pricing page publishes no charge for them.
Plan allowance: Hobby is $0/month with a one-time $100 usage credit and 20 concurrent sandboxes.
open_questions: The 1 vCPU row prints $0.000016/s, but the 2, 4, 6 and 8 vCPU rows print $0.000028, $0.000056, $0.000084 and $0.000112, which is $0.000014 per vCPU-second. The page does not print a per-vCPU rate, so the 1 vCPU price is used as the unit rate here, and larger sizes should be priced from their own rows.
The page marks 2 vCPU and 4 GiB as [Default], while earlier billing docs said default resources are 2 vCPU / 512 MiB; the docs were not re-read here.
The page never says in words whether the meter is allocated or used CPU and RAM; both tables are keyed by configured size, so allocation is assumed.
Whether the $100 Hobby credit expires: it is described only as one-time.
Charges for egress, template builds and template storage are not published on this page; absence is not confirmation that they are free.
